proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) and suppose \(d_e(G)<\infty\).  Then \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\) by the definition of \(d_e\).  Multiplying the defining covariance identity on the left by \((I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\) and on the right by \(I_n-\Lambda\) gives
\[
 \Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).
\tag{1}
\]
Thus every disturbance coordinate lies in \(K_G(\lambda_D)\).  The reverse inclusion of generators is immediate from \(K_G\subseteq L\) and \(\lambda_D\subseteq L\), so
\[
 L=K_G(\lambda_D).
\tag{2}
\]

Choose \(U\subseteq\lambda_D\setminus\{\lambda_e\}\) maximal algebraically independent over \(K_G\), put \(F=K_G(U)\), and enumerate
\[
 y=(y_1,\ldots,y_q)=\lambda_D\setminus U.
\]
Because \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\), it cannot enlarge the algebraically independent set \(U\).  Maximality of \(U\), followed by adjoining the finitely many coordinates in \(y\), therefore makes \(L/F\) finite.  It is separable because \(F\) has characteristic zero.  The minimal polynomial \(p(t)\in K_G[t]\) of \(\lambda_e\) remains irreducible over \(F=K_G(U)\).  Indeed, a nontrivial factorization over \(K_G(U)\) could be cleared of its finitely many denominators; because \(U\) is algebraically independent and the infinite field \(K_G\) contains \(\mathbb C\), one could then specialize \(U\) to a point of \(K_G^{|U|}\) where all denominators and both leading coefficients are nonzero.  The specialization would be a nontrivial factorization of \(p\) in \(K_G[t]\), a contradiction.  Consequently
\[
 [F(\lambda_e):F]=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=d_e(G).
\tag{3}
\]

By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) and \(\mathrm{def:generic\mbox{-}fiber}\), localizing first at \(S_G\) and then at the nonzero elements of \(K_G[U]\) gives an evaluation homomorphism
\[
 F[y_1,\ldots,y_q]\longrightarrow L
\]
whose kernel is generated by the missing-bidirected residuals \(F_{ij}\).  If \(g_a\in F[t]\) is the minimal polynomial of \(y_a\), there are polynomials \(c_{a,ij}\in F[y]\) such that
\[
 g_a(y_a)=\sum_{i\leftrightarrow j\notin B}c_{a,ij}(y)F_{ij}(y).
\tag{4}
\]
Differentiate (4) and evaluate in \(L\).  Since every residual vanishes, this gives
\[
 g_a'(y_a)\,dy_a
 =\sum_{i\leftrightarrow j\notin B}c_{a,ij}(y)\,dF_{ij}.
\tag{5}
\]
Separability gives \(g_a'(y_a)\ne0\), so the evaluated residual gradients span all \(dy_a\).  The residual Jacobian with respect to \(y\) therefore has rank \(q\).  Select residuals \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\) with nonzero Jacobian determinant \(\Delta\in L\).

There are exactly \(d_e(G)\) distinct \(F\)-embeddings of \(F(\lambda_e)\) into an algebraic closure \(\overline F\), by (3) and separability.  Each extends to an \(F\)-embedding of the finite algebraic extension \(L/F\): adjoin the remaining algebraic generators one at a time and, at each step, send the next generator to any root in \(\overline F\) of the transported minimal polynomial.  Every extension is a common zero of \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\), and it sends the nonzero field element \(\Delta\) to a nonzero element.  It is therefore a nonsingular isolated zero of the selected square system.  Embeddings with different restrictions to \(F(\lambda_e)\) have distinct \(\lambda_e\)-coordinates.

Partition the variables \(y\) into nonempty blocks indexed by their child vertices, and let \(r_v\) be the size of block \(v\).  Then
\[
 1\leq r_v\leq\operatorname{indeg}_D(v).
\tag{6}
\]
The displayed formula for \(F_{ij}\) is affine-linear in each of the two child blocks indexed by \(i,j\).  Thus a selected residual meeting one remaining block is unary, and one meeting two remaining blocks is bilinear with multidegree at most one in each block.  Decompose the equation-block incidence graph of the selected square system into connected components.  A nonzero monomial in \(\Delta\) supplies a row-to-column matching, so each component contains equally many equations and variables.

Consider the component containing \(\lambda_e\).  Suppose it contains \(b\) variable blocks, \(u\) unary equations, and \(m_H\) binary equations.  If \(b>1\), the binary equations form a connected simple graph \(H\) on the blocks: connectivity follows from the choice of component, and simplicity follows because there is only one residual for an unordered pair of distinct child vertices.  If \(b=1\), take \(H\) to be the one-vertex graph.  Since the component is square,
\[
 \sum_{v\in V(H)}r_v=u+m_H.
\tag{7}
\]

The multihomogeneous bound \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\) bounds the number of isolated zeros of this component by the coefficient of \(\prod_vX_v^{r_v}\) in
\[
 \left(\prod_{\ell=1}^{u}X_{v(\ell)}\right)
 \left(\prod_{\{v,w\}\in E(H)}(X_v+X_w)\right).
\tag{8}
\]
After subtracting the fixed unary exponents, (8) is \(c_H(s)\) for one prescribed nonnegative indegree vector \(s\); if a coordinate of \(s\) is negative, the coefficient is zero and cannot bound the already exhibited solutions, so the relevant coefficient has \(s\geq0\).  Every conjugate of \(\lambda_e\) supplies a distinct isolated zero in this component.  Hence
\[
 d_e(G)\leq c_H(s).
\tag{9}
\]

A finite acyclic directed graph has a source: otherwise repeatedly following an incoming arrow would repeat a vertex and create a directed cycle.  The root of the supplied arborescence has no incoming directed edge, since an arrow into it together with its tree path to the arrow's tail would create a cycle.  In particular at least one vertex has no nonempty child block, so
\[
 b\leq n-1.
\tag{10}
\]
Write \(g_H=m_H-b+1\) when \(b>1\), and set \(g_H=0\) when \(b=1\).  For \(b>1\), (6)--(7) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 g_H
 &=\sum_{v\in V(H)}r_v-u-b+1\\
 &\leq\sum_{v\in V(H)}\bigl(\operatorname{indeg}_D(v)-1\bigr)+1\\
 &\leq\sum_{v\ne\operatorname{root}(T)}
       \bigl(\operatorname{indeg}_D(v)-1\bigr)+1\\
 &=|D|-n+2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
The second inequality uses \(\mathrm{ass:arborescence}\): every nonroot vertex has one incoming tree arrow, so each omitted summand is nonnegative, while the root has indegree zero as just proved.  For \(b=1\), \(g_H=0\leq |D|-n+2\), because \(T\subseteq D\) and \(|T|=n-1\).  Thus (9)--(11) and \(\mathrm{def:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\) yield
\[
 d_e(G)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,\,|D|-n+2}.
\tag{12}
\]

Because \(T\subseteq D\) and \(|T|=n-1\), the excess-budget assumption gives
\[
 |D|-n+2=|D\setminus T|+1\leq k+1.
\tag{13}
\]
Monotonicity and \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\) now give
\[
 d_e(G)
 \leq\vartheta_{n-1,\,|D|-n+2}
 \leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}
 \leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\},
\tag{14}
\]
and applying the same lemma before (13) gives
\[
 d_e(G)\leq\min\{2^{|D|-n+2},\tau_{n-1}\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Maximizing (12)--(14) over all finite-degree members of \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) proves
\[
 D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}.
\tag{16}
\]
No step required the other components of the generic fiber to be zero-dimensional.

For \(n=6\), the exact recurrence table in \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
 \vartheta_{5,3}=6,\qquad
 \vartheta_{5,4}=8,\qquad
 \vartheta_{5,5}=12,\qquad
 \vartheta_{5,g}=24\quad(g\geq6).
\]
Substitution of \(g=k+1\) into (16) proves
\[
 D_2(6)\leq6,\qquad D_3(6)\leq8,\qquad D_4(6)\leq12,
 \qquad D_k(6)\leq24\quad(k\geq5),
\]
for every admissible \(k\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq0\), the joint orientation frontier is finite, is nondecreasing in each argument, and satisfies
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\qquad\text{whenever }N\geq2g+1.
\]
For five available vertices the exact finite recurrence values are
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24),
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{5,g}=24\quad(g\geq6).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a fixed connected simple graph \(H\), choosing \(X_i\) from the factor indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(i\).  Consequently \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) with indegree vector \(r\).  Only finitely many labeled simple graphs on at most \(N\) vertices and finitely many orientations of each graph occur, so the maximum defining \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) is finite.  Enlarging \(N\) or \(g\) enlarges the feasible collection, proving monotonicity.

Fix a spanning tree \(S\) of \(H\), and write \(b=|V(H)|\).  There are
\[
 |E(H)\setminus E(S)|=|E(H)|-(b-1)=g(H)
\]
non-tree edges.  For a prescribed indegree vector \(r\), fix orientations of those \(g(H)\) edges.  There is at most one compatible orientation of \(S\): at a leaf of the current tree, the required residual indegree forces the orientation of its unique remaining tree edge, after which that leaf may be deleted; induction on the number of vertices proves uniqueness.  Therefore
\[
 c_H(r)\leq2^{g(H)}\leq2^g.
\tag{1}
\]
The established fixed-edge completion in \(\mathrm{lem:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}ceiling}\) also gives \(c_H(r)\leq\tau_N\) whenever \(b\leq N\).  Taking the maximum over \(H,r\) proves
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\tag{2}
\]

For the reverse inequality in the stated range, first let \(g=0\).  The included one-vertex graph gives \(\vartheta_{N,0}\geq1=2^0\), which combines with (1).  Now let \(g\geq1\).  Form a bouquet of \(g\) triangles by taking a central vertex \(z\), two new vertices \(u_i,v_i\) for each \(1\leq i\leq g\), and the three edges
\[
 \{z,u_i\},\quad\{u_i,v_i\},\quad\{v_i,z\}
\]
for each \(i\).  This connected simple graph has \(2g+1\) vertices, \(3g\) edges, and hence cyclomatic number
\[
 3g-(2g+1)+1=g.
\]
Orient each triangle as either of its two directed cycles.  Every such choice has indegree \(g\) at \(z\) and indegree one at every \(u_i,v_i\).  The choices are independent across triangles, so for
\[
 r_z=g,\qquad r_{u_i}=r_{v_i}=1
\]
the score fiber contains \(2^g\) orientations.  Thus \(\vartheta_{N,g}\geq2^g\) when \(N\geq2g+1\), and (1) proves equality.

For completeness, the five-vertex values are certified by the following finite coefficient recurrence.  Given a labeled graph \(H\) with lexicographically ordered edges \(e_j=\{u_j,v_j\}\), define
\[
 A_{H,0}(r)=\mathbf 1\{r=0\},
 \qquad
 A_{H,j}(r)=A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{u_j})
             +A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{v_j}),
\tag{3}
\]
where a term with a negative coordinate is zero.  Expanding one factor at a time proves by induction that
\[
 A_{H,|E(H)|}(r)=c_H(r).
\tag{4}
\]
Put \(\mu(H)=\max_r c_H(r)\), and let \(N_{b,m}(s)\) be the number of connected labeled graphs on \([b]\) with \(m\) edges and \(\mu(H)=s\).  Applying the additions in (3) to every subset of the at most ten possible edges gives the following complete audit table; within a row, \(N(s)\) abbreviates \(N_{b,m}(s)\), and a blank entry is zero:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l|c}
b&m&\{s:N_{b,m}(s)\ne0\}&\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\\ \hline
1&0&N(1)=1&1\\
2&1&N(1)=1&1\\
3&2&N(1)=3&3\\
3&3&N(2)=1&1\\
4&3&N(1)=16&16\\
4&4&N(2)=15&15\\
4&5&N(3)=6&6\\
4&6&N(4)=1&1\\
5&4&N(1)=125&125\\
5&5&N(2)=222&222\\
5&6&N(3)=190,\ N(4)=15&205\\
5&7&N(4)=50,\ N(5)=60,\ N(6)=10&120\\
5&8&N(7)=15,\ N(8)=30&45\\
5&9&N(12)=10&10\\
5&10&N(24)=1&1
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
This table is independently checkable without graph-isomorphism choices: scan the edge subsets in lexicographic order, reject a subset unless a search from vertex \(1\) reaches all \(b\) vertices, and use (3).  As an arithmetic checksum, if \(a_{b,m}=\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\), decomposition by the connected component containing vertex \(1\) gives
\[
 a_{1,0}=1,
 \qquad
 a_{b,m}=\binom{\binom b2}{m}
 -\sum_{q=1}^{b-1}\binom{b-1}{q-1}
   \sum_{\ell=0}^{m}a_{q,\ell}
   \binom{\binom{b-q}{2}}{m-\ell}.
\tag{6}
\]
Substitution in (6) gives exactly the last column of (5).

The maxima in the seven five-vertex rows are attained explicitly.  Let
\[
 S=\{12,13,14,15\},
\]
and, for \(0\leq h\leq6\), let \(H_h\) have edge set \(S\cup A_h\), where the following table also gives a score vector whose coefficient is maximal:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|c|c}
h&A_h&r&c_{H_h}(r)\\ \hline
0&\varnothing&(4,0,0,0,0)&1\\
1&\{23\}&(3,1,1,0,0)&2\\
2&\{25,34\}&(2,1,1,1,1)&4\\
3&\{23,24,25\}&(2,2,1,1,1)&6\\
4&\{23,24,25,34\}&(2,2,2,1,1)&8\\
5&\{23,24,25,34,35\}&(2,2,2,2,1)&12\\
6&\{23,24,25,34,35,45\}&(2,2,2,2,2)&24
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
Each coefficient in (7) follows by the same seven-or-fewer applications of (3) after the four star edges have been processed.  Since a connected graph with \(b\) vertices and \(m\) edges has cyclomatic number \(m-b+1\), (5) supplies the upper bounds and (7) supplies matching lower bounds for every \(0\leq g\leq6\).  Hence
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24).
\]
Finally a simple graph on at most five vertices has cyclomatic number at most
\[
 \binom52-5+1=6.
\]
Thus increasing \(g\) beyond six adds no feasible graph, and \(\vartheta_{5,g}=24\) for every \(g\geq6\).

For the remaining unsettled regime \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), use \(\mathsf{FrontierHandle}\) to determine an explicit formula or finite structural recurrence solely in \(n,k\) for \(D_k(n)\). \[
 2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}
 \leq D_k(n)
 \leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\qquad(n\geq4),
\]
agree with

 D_0(2)=1,\qquad D_k(3)=1,\qquad D_k(4)=2,

 D_0(6)=2,\qquad D_1(6)=4,\qquad D_2(6)\leq6,

The identity \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) for \(N\geq2g+1\) explains the same combinatorial elbow as the established SEM equality threshold, since \(N=n-1\) and \(g=k+1\); the SEM equality itself comes from the one-sink construction. proposed.name: vartheta_Ng
proposed.def: \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) is the maximum prescribed-indegree orientation-fiber cardinality among connected simple labeled graphs on at most \(N\) vertices and with cyclomatic number at most \(g\), as specified in \(\mathrm{def:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The strengthened upper theorem requires a symbol for the maximum orientation fiber jointly constrained by vertex count and cyclomatic number.

proposed.name: Joint vertex/cycle-rank orientation frontier
proposed.construction:
For integers \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq0\), let \(H\) range over connected simple graphs on a labeled vertex set \([b]\), where \(1\leq b\leq N\), and whose cyclomatic number is
\[
 g(H)=|E(H)|-b+1\leq g.
\]
For \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_b)\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^{b}\), put
\[
 c_H(r)=[X_1^{r_1}\cdots X_b^{r_b}]
          \prod_{\{i,j\}\in E(H)}(X_i+X_j),
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{N,g}:=\max_{H,r}c_H(r).
\]
The one-vertex graph is included: its empty product is \(1\), its cyclomatic number is zero, and \(c_H(0)=1\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition couples the two structural restrictions that hold simultaneously for the query component.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine the exact value of \(D_k(n)\) for every positive \(k\) with \(n\geq6\) and \(n<2k+4\), construct attaining graph-query families, and prove that one original directed coefficient separates the generic branches.
obligation.obstruction: The quantity \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) is a universal combinatorial ceiling, but no proved result realizes its extremizers throughout the remaining strip after forced covariance relations, exact \(S_G\)-localization, affine dehomogenization, and projective-infinity losses are imposed.
obligation.attempted: I coupled block count and cycle rank in one orientation frontier, proved its spanning-tree cap, triangle-bouquet elbow, and exact five-vertex recurrence, and combined these with the one-sink equality region, the inherited lower envelope, and the exact small-size table. These arguments sharpen the six-vertex ceiling but do not construct or exclude SEM extremizers in the remaining strip.
obligation.partial_result:
The projection-aware theorem now proves, for every \(n\geq4\),
\[
 2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}
 \leq D_k(n)
 \leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}
 \leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}.
\]
The finite recurrence gives \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), hence
\[
 D_0(6)=2,\quad D_1(6)=4,\quad D_2(6)\leq6,\quad
 D_3(6)\leq8,\quad D_4(6)\leq12,\quad D_k(6)\leq24\ (k\geq5).
\]
The exact table through five vertices remains \(D_0(2)=1\), \(D_k(3)=1\), \(D_k(4)=2\), \(D_0(5)=2\), \(D_1(5)=3\), and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\).  Moreover \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) whenever \(n\geq2k+4\).  The combinatorial elbow \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) for \(N\geq2g+1\) matches that threshold after setting \(N=n-1\) and \(g=k+1\), but no SEM attainment of \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) is proved in the remaining strip.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\). For \(n\geq4\), the proved two-sided envelope is \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). The exact five-vertex orientation recurrence is \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), giving \(D_2(6)\leq6\), \(D_3(6)\leq8\), \(D_4(6)\leq12\), and \(D_k(6)\leq24\) for admissible \(k\geq5\); the established equalities are \(D_0(6)=2\) and \(D_1(6)=4\). Exact equality \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) holds when \(n\geq2k+4\), and the exact table is \(D_0(2)=1\), \(D_k(3)=1\), \(D_k(4)=2\), \(D_0(5)=2\), \(D_1(5)=3\), and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\). At zero excess the dispatcher returns the exact published \(1/2/\infty\) tree classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions; at positive excess its unconditional algebraic branch retains the explicit computable report \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\) and does not claim to compute \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\). A rational-circuit representation of \(p_e(t)\) is delivered only under the valid-chart and successful-output conditions of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).

prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\), where \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) maximizes prescribed-indegree orientation fibers jointly over at most \(N\) vertices and cycle rank at most \(g\). Its exact five-vertex recurrence gives \((1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), hence the new six-vertex caps \(6,8,12,24\). The combinatorial elbow \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) for \(N\geq2g+1\) matches the established SEM equality threshold \(n\geq2k+4\); the exact frontier is also known through five vertices, but \(\vartheta\) is not claimed SEM-attained in the unresolved strip. The zero-excess dispatcher retains the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions; positive excess retains the existing efficiently reportable size-binomial cap, while exact polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference remain chart-conditional.

project_justification.fill: The paper proves the coupled projection-aware envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\) for \(n\geq4\). It gives a checkable finite recurrence \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), the resulting six-vertex row, the structural elbow \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) for \(N\geq2g+1\), the large-size SEM equality, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It isolates the remaining positive-\(k\), \(n\geq6\) small-size frontier without claiming that the combinatorial ceiling is SEM-attained there. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), the exact frontier remains between \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\) and \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\). The latter is only a combinatorial ceiling: SEM branches may be lost through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The six-vertex recurrence sharpens the former cap to \(6,8,12,24\) for \(k=2,3,4,\geq5\), respectively, but no attaining SEM family is asserted. The unconditional fixed-parameter dispatcher retains the efficiently explicit size-binomial cap because this round supplies no uniform exact computation and certificate for \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) within its runtime. The exhaustive five-node orbit census remains a secondary regression and coordinate-census question because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). On the certified event determined by a supplied valid source-prime chart, the exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition hold. Their chart antecedent appears in every statement; no chart-free statistical theorem is asserted. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, and the coupled ceiling \(D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). The exact recurrence \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\) yields \(D_2(6)\leq6\), \(D_3(6)\leq8\), \(D_4(6)\leq12\), and \(D_k(6)\leq24\) for admissible \(k\geq5\), alongside the established \(D_0(6)=2\) and \(D_1(6)=4\). The combinatorial elbow matches the large-size threshold, but the joint orientation ceiling is not claimed SEM-attained in the remaining positive-excess strip. Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the efficiently available ceiling \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\); it does not compute \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\), \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts and successful output, the conditional geometric-resolution theorem returns the exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. On precisely that same conditional domain, the exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.
